heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Prusament PETG exceptionally well out of the box, utilizing its direct drive extruder to achieve reliable speeds up to 179 mm/s capped at a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Because PETG requires no chamber heating and Prusament PETG is non-abrasive, the stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame design are fully production-ready without hardware modifications.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of glue stick or specialized release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s under the Filament > Advanced tab to prevent under-extrusion at high linear speeds.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' and set a max detour length to reduce fine stringing across exterior cosmetic surfaces.
Increase Pressure Advance to 0.036 (tune via OrcaSlicer PA tower calibration) to prevent corner bulging typical of viscous PETG.
Set the First Layer Height to 0.24mm and First Layer Flow Ratio to 0.98 to avoid PETG sticking to the nozzle tip and dragging.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair buildup on nozzle
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Prusament PETG has absorbed ambient moisture, lowering melt viscosity and causing post-retraction ooze.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 65°C for 6 hours before printing, and increase retraction speed to 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Tearing of PEI coating on print removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds aggressively to smooth or unconditioned PEI surfaces via chemical cross-linking.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Always apply a thin interface layer of PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive on the Textured PEI Plate before printing, and let the bed cool below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer splitting or weak layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extrusion before polymer chains can interlock.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower maximum part cooling fan speed to 40% and disable the auxiliary side fan completely in the cooling settings.

faq.question: Does printing Prusament PETG on the P1P require an enclosure?
faq.answer: No, PETG does not require an enclosure and prints best in open-air setups where ambient temperatures remain moderate to prevent heat creep in the cold end.

faq.question: Can the stock stainless steel nozzle handle Prusament PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, standard Prusament PETG is non-abrasive and will not cause premature wear on the stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Why does PETG stick to the nozzle tip and ruin the first layer?
faq.answer: PETG has high affinity for metals; if squished too aggressively into the bed, excess molten plastic curls onto the nozzle. Raise Z-offset slightly or reduce first layer flow to 0.98.

faq.question: What build plate temperature works best for Prusament PETG on the P1P?
faq.answer: Set the bed temperature to 80°C for the first layer and 83°C for subsequent layers on the Textured PEI plate to prevent warping while maintaining good adhesion.
